pages.x: In 1754 a young Virginia militia officer, George Washington, ambushed a French scouting party in the woods of Pennsylvania. Britain and France both claimed the Ohio valley, and the shots in that glen helped set off a war around the world.
In Europe, old enemies swapped partners: Austria joined France against Prussia, and Britain backed Prussia. In 1756 Frederick the Great of Prussia struck first and invaded Saxony.

Frederick fought Austria, France, Russia and Sweden at once. He won brilliant victories at Rossbach and Leuthen in 1757, but by 1761 he was close to defeat, his army shrinking and Berlin raided twice.

In India, the East India Company's Robert Clive, with about 3,000 men, beat the Nawab of Bengal's army of 50,000 at Plassey in 1757, mostly by bribing the Nawab's commander to stand aside. The Company was on its way to ruling Bengal.

In 1759, Britain's year of victories, General James Wolfe's men climbed a cliff by night to the Plains of Abraham outside Quebec. Wolfe and the French commander, Montcalm, were both killed in the battle that followed, and New France was lost.

In January 1762 Frederick's deadliest enemy, Empress Elizabeth of Russia, died. Her successor, Peter III, adored Frederick and made peace at once. Frederick called it the miracle of the House of Brandenburg.
Soldiers died in battle, and far more of disease, while armies stripped the land. Prussia alone may have lost a tenth of its people.

In 1763 France gave Canada and the lands east of the Mississippi to Britain, and Spain gave up Florida, while France kept its sugar islands. Prussia kept Silesia. Britain was now the leading power in the world, but deep in debt.

Winston Churchill called it the first world war. It made Britain master of North America and India and Prussia a great power. But the taxes Britain then put on its American colonies to pay for it led straight to the American Revolution.
pts: Its debts led to the American Revolution
